h1: High Blood Pressure is a Silent Killer

blocks.alt: Blood pressure monitor with high blood pressure reading

blocks.html: Hypertension, or high blood pressure, is when the force of blood against the artery walls is too high. It can lead to severe complications and increases the risk of heart disease, stroke, and death.
When your blood pressure is too high, you can develop symptoms. If you are aware that you have been diagnosed with hypertension, you should watch out for these symptoms:

items: Severe Headache
Fatigue or Confusion
Vision Problems
Chest Pain
Difficulty Breathing
Irregular Heartbeat
Pounding in your chest, neck, or ears.
Nosebleeds

blocks.html: You can have high blood pressure and also experience no obvious symptoms until it is too late and you experience a stroke or a heart attack. It is very important to monitor your blood pressure regularly.

Hypertension is best diagnosed by having your blood pressure measured. Your doctor may also review your medical history as well as conduct a physical examination. A consistent blood pressure 140/90 mm Hg or higher is considered high blood pressure.

blocks.text: Common Supplements Found in Our Pharmacy to Help Combat Symptoms

blocks.html: Magnesium  Magnesium deficiency is the second most common deficiency in the U.S. and returning your magnesium levels to normal has been proven to help regulate blood pressure.
Omega-3 Fatty Acids Taking these offer a wide variety of health benefits including the ability to reduce blood pressure by reducing the LDL, or bad cholesterol.

Coenzyme Q10 is crucial for energy production. Coenzyme Q10 (aka CoQ10) is an antioxidant necessary for proper cell function, found in every cell of the body. Your cells need CoQ10 to produce energy, and research shows that it benefits patients with cardiovascular disease.
L-Citrulline is a pre-Arginine supplement but it’s more easily absorbed by the body than arginine. It helps improve the Nitrogen balance of the blood, which improves circulation.
Folate/Folic Acid (both forms of Vitamin B9) have been shown to reduce the incidence of strokes in adults with hypertension.

Hypertension can often be controlled by medications prescribed by your Victory Medical physician and taken regularly. In addition to such, there are ways one can control their hypertension. Ways to help control your hypertension in addition to medication or even preventing it are:

items: Lose extra weight to control your waistline.
Eat a healthy diet
Reduce sodium in your diet
Limit the amount of alcohol you drink
Cut back on caffeine
Reduce your stress
Exercise regularly
Quit smoking.
